summary: Discovery focused on failover topologies and SLA alignment across Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Customer stressed requirement for sub-100ms p95 latency under normal load, predictable degradation during incidents, multi-region failover, and strong auditability (SOC2/SAML/KMS). Agreed to follow-ups: share SLA appendix, sizing for Dedicated, and run a 48-hour failover sim in staging.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros? I'm Jordan, AE at Redwood.
[00:10] Marta: Hi, Marta Delgado, Head of ML at Apex Security. We're evaluating inference platforms for our customer-facing agent.
[00:18] Ethan: Ethan Shaw, Platform eng, responsible for infra and runbooks.
[00:23] Lian: Lian Zhou, security architect.
[00:27] Priya: Priya Raman, infra SE at Redwood, I'll cover failover and dedicated sizing.
[00:34] Jordan: Goal for today — understand your SLOs and incident tolerance so we can recommend Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
[00:45] Marta: Right. Our main non-negotiables: p95 under 100ms for short context calls (<512 tokens)  and degradation behavior that we can predict. Also we need full audit logs, KMS integration, and we can't have customer data egressed outside EU for some workloads.
[01:10] Priya: Got it. For p95 targets we usually look at runtime on the model, batching policy, and region placement. Hosted can hit sub-100ms p95 for smaller models and low seq length; Dedicated gives more predictability at scale. For regional constraints we can pin deployments to eu-west1 or run Private in your VPC.
[01:35] Ethan: If we go Dedicated, what's the fallback when a zone goes down? Do you do multi-region routing automatically?
[01:42] Priya: We support smart routing policies. You can configure primary region eu-west1 with a fallback to eu-west2 or a cold warm in us-central depending on data residency constraints. Failover can be synchronous (active-active) or async (active-passive). Active-active gives lower failover latency but requires cross-region KV sync which has consistency tradeoffs.
[02:05] Marta: Explain KV sync and the impact on the prefix cache — we saw some notes about "KV cache" being eventual sometimes in docs and it worried us.
[02:12] Priya: Sure. The KV cache (prefix or chat cache) stores recent generation state to make repeated calls fast. In an active-active multi-region setup we replicate KV state via a bounded replication stream. Under network partitions there's a window where the other region might not have the latest KV entries, so warm-up latencies go up. We recommend cache warming strategies during failover and we also support prefix caching on the client to mitigate.
[02:40] Lian: For compliance, we need to know what is logged and retained. Is everything token-level logged? How is PII redaction handled?
[02:48] Jordan: By default we log metadata: request id, model version, latency, and aggregate token counts. Full transcripts can be logged but are optional; for Private deployments you control retention, KMS keys, and can enable HSM for key ops. We can provide our SOC2 Type II report and the audit log schema.
[03:05] Marta: Can you talk SLA? We need a 99.9% availability target and clear definitions for partial degradation.
[03:12] Priya: Our Dedicated SLA covers uptime of the compute plane — we have regional SLAs and can offer 99.9% with Reserved capacity. For partial degradation, we define a degraded state when p95 exceeds threshold or error rates exceed X%. We have pre-configured fallback policies: downgrade to a quantized model variant, route to a cheaper lower-capacity pool, or serve cached responses. You can pick an ordered policy with automatic rollbacks.
[03:40] Ethan: How do automatic rollbacks work? Are they safe for stateful sessions?
[03:46] Priya: Rollbacks are model-level: if a newer model variant increases error rate, we can route a percentage back to the stable model and gradually shift. For stateful sessions with KV cache, we provide sticky routing so ongoing sessions remain pinned to the node or region until session ends, otherwise we risk cache misses.
[04:06] Marta: Ok, for our conversational bot we care about session continuity more than absolute latency spikes during failover. Is sticky routing compatible with multi-region failover?
[04:14] Priya: Yes, but there's a tradeoff. Sticky routing preserves session state but can delay failover if the pinned node is unhealthy. We have policies that allow time-limited stickiness and forced rebind after timeout to enable recovery.
[04:29] Ethan: On the network side, what about DNS vs Anycast-based routing?
[04:33] Priya: We use a combination. For Hosted we provide global Anycast endpoints with regional backends and health checks. For Dedicated/Private you can plug in your DNS-based weighted routing or use our region-aware LB. Health checks and circuit-breaking are part of the routing layer.
[04:50] Lian: Encryption in flight and at rest — do you support customer-managed KMS?
[04:54] Jordan: Yes, CMK supported for Private and Dedicated; Hosted supports bring-your-own-key for some enterprise tiers. We can map out the KMS options in the SLA appendix.
[05:04] Marta: We run spikes — burst QPS up to 8x baseline for 10-12 minutes. How does that affect failover and cost?
[05:12] Priya: For bursts we recommend autoscale + burst capacity on Dedicated or a hybrid: primary Dedicated with Hosted fallback for excess traffic. Cost-wise fallback to Hosted uses on-demand pools which are more expensive per-token but keep latency bounded. We'll model costs in the sizing doc.
[05:30] Ethan: Is the failover deterministic? We want to script the sim and expect repeatable outcomes.
[05:34] Priya: We can run deterministic failover simulations in staging — we have a "chaos run" playbook that can simulate regional outage, degraded network, and cold-start traffic. We'll share the runbook and can execute with your team.
[05:48] Marta: Great. Also want to validate quotas and soft-limits so we don't hit silent throttles during spike tests.
[05:55] Jordan: We'll share quota docs and show how rate limiting and circuit-breakers are surfaced in the Console.
[06:02] Ethan: For metrics, what granularities do you expose? Per-route p50/p95/p99, cost per token, error breakdown?
[06:08] Priya: Yes, Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, error types, model rollouts, and tracing hooks. You can pull these via API for alerting.
[06:18] Marta: Any gotchas with Private on-prem? We might want air-gapped for EU-sensitivity customers.
[06:24] Priya: Private supports air-gapped installs but upgrades and telemetry require an offline package process. Auditability is higher but ops burden increases. Also certain autoscaling behaviors are limited when there's no cloud control plane — we provide an operator playbook.
[06:40] Ethan: About degradation strategies — you mentioned quantized model fallback. How much quality loss should we expect?
[06:46] Priya: It depends on model family. Typical 4-bit quantization for a conversational model can increase hallucination risk slightly; we recommend guardrails via safety prompts and post-rerankers. For many intents precision is similar; for nuanced QA we suggest using fallback to a smaller but full-precision variant instead of aggressive quant.
[07:05] Marta: Can you support A/B rollouts for fallback policies? We want to test degradation policy effectiveness before promoting globally.
[07:12] Priya: Yes, rollouts can be policy-based: e.g., 10% traffic to quantized fallback, monitor metrics, increase. Also can tie to user cohorts.
[07:20] Jordan: Let's talk timeline. Marta, what are you driving?
[07:24] Marta: We're shortlisting vendors this month. Pilot needs to start early March; production by mid-April.
[07:30] Jordan: Okay we can aim to have pricing, SLA appendix, and a Dedicated sizing by Feb 18 to slot a 48-hour sim the week of Feb 23.
[07:38] Lian: One more security Q — SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning?
[07:42] Jordan: Supported. We'll attach the SSO configuration guide.
[07:45] Ethan: Any performance artifacts you can share? We asked for benchmarks earlier.
[07:49] Priya: We'll attach a perf matrix showing p50/p95 for reference models at various seq lengths and hardware profiles — plus guidance on batch size tradeoffs.
[07:58] Marta: Cool. Can we get an example incident playbook for a partial zone outage?
[08:02] Priya: Yes, the failover playbook with run commands, health-check thresholds, and rollback steps will be included.
[08:10] Jordan: Recap of next steps: Jordan will send SLA + SOC2 + pricing, Priya will prepare sizing and failover runbook, Apex will share QPS histograms. We'll schedule the 48-hour sim. Any objections?
[08:24] Marta: No, sounds good. Thanks.
[08:27] Ethan: Thanks everyone.
[08:30] Lian: Thanks.
[08:33] [END]
